transcript.text: It could be as simple as a clogged filter, a full dustbin, or a jammed brush bar stopping the motor from running. To help narrow it down, please start by checking the brush area for any hair or thread tangles that might be holding it back. With the vacuum switched off and unplugged (or battery removed), turn the floorhead over and try spinning the roller by hand to see if it moves freely.
its not the brush. theres no power at all, the motor doesnt even start. i cant turn it over anyway, my back

Since there is no power at all and it won't switch on, the issue is likely with the electrical supply rather than the motor itself. For cordless models, a flat or failed battery is often the usual culprit, while for corded ones, it could be the plug fuse or mains cable. Please check if the charging light comes on when you place it on its dock (or try plugging it into a different socket) to see if it’s receiving power. Also, ensure the on/off switch isn’t stuck or damaged.
its a plugged in one, not cordless. the lamp works in the same socket so its not the socket. the switch clicks normally i think

Since the socket has power and the switch clicks normally, we need to look at what connects them. Please check along the length of the mains cable for any cuts or damage, and if your plug has a fuse, ensure it hasn't blown (you can swap it with a known good one). If those are fine, please provide the make and model number so I can give specific advice; this is usually on a label on the body, often under the bin.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
theres black tape on the cable near the plug, my son did it ages ago, and its a bit bent there. i dont have a screwdriver or spare fuse. its a red Henry, i cant read the label or turn it over

The black tape and bent cable near the plug are very likely causing this "no power" issue by breaking the electrical connection inside. Since you can't replace the fuse or open the unit, please try carefully bending the cable at that taped section while the vacuum is switched on to see if it briefly starts working. If it does, that suggests a broken wire in the mains lead which will need replacing for safety. You can find the model number on a label under the dustbin once you've managed to tip it over safely.
no im not doing that again, it flickered on once when i moved the wire and it frightened me. is it safe to use?

It is not safe to use because the flickering indicates a broken wire inside the cable, which could cause a short circuit or fire. Since you cannot fix the mains lead yourself without tools, the vacuum needs a new cable or professional repair. You can find the model number on a label under the dustbin once you've managed to tip it over safely for future reference.
